Subject: Stakeholder mapping & procurement paths - ACME Commerce

Hi Sofia — great to talk earlier. Thanks for walking us through the use case and traffic patterns for the personalized search feature. Quick recap and asks below so we’re all aligned.

Call recap (high level):
- Goal: reduce search latency and cost for personalized recommendations during peak retail hours (Black Friday prep).
- Primary workloads: short-form query generation + reranking; steady-state traffic with 5-8x spikes during campaigns.
- Success metrics: P95 latency < 120ms, 30–40% lower per-token cost vs current managed endpoints.

Key open items / asks:
1) Stakeholder map: who is the economic buyer (e.g., SVP Product / CFO), and who will own procurement / legal / security sign-off?
2) Procurement process: timeline, required docs (SOW/PO, security questionnaire, SOC2 evidence), and typical contract redline owners.
3) Org chart or decision chain: an org PDF or a short email that points us to the right people to loop in.
4) Any strict data residency or IP requirements (e.g., cannot send PII to third-party cloud).

Next steps I propose:
- If you can share an org chart or list of names/roles, I’ll put together a targeted plan for stakeholders and a one-pager for procurement.
- I’ll send an updated post-call recap with a sample mutual action plan and an estimated SOW cadence once we have the procurement path.

Thanks — I’ve looped Monica (Customer Success) and Vivek (Solutions) so they can prepare a short technical appendix and a procurement-ready checklist.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the recap.

Quick answers to your asks:
- Economic buyer: Eduardo Martinez (SVP Product) — he owns the product budget for commerce initiatives.
- Procurement/legal/security: Daniel Cho (Head of Procurement) handles vendor contracting; Legal will review on standard terms (I’ll intro if needed). Security will validate data flows — point person is Priya Natarajan (security engineering).
- Data residency: Primary data must stay in us-west and EU for EU customers; we can discuss exact PII constraints during security review.

I’m attaching the org chart and our procurement intake doc to this thread to speed things up.

I’ve copied Daniel so he’s aware — Daniel, would you confirm the procurement timeline and whether we need an NDA before SOW?

Hi all — thanks for looping me in. Quick notes from procurement side:
- Typical timeline: procurement + legal review usually takes 3–5 weeks for standard SaaS/SWE vendor SOWs; can be shorter if there’s an approved vendor list.
- Required docs: W-9/COI, SOW, Master Services Agreement (MSA) + Data Processing Addendum (for EU data). We’ll also request SOC 2 report and encryption details.
- NDA: not necessary at this stage; we can exchange an NDA if Redwood prefers — otherwise we usually start with a standard MSA and SOW.

Action for Rishi: please send a simple procurement packet (one-pager with scope, estimated costs, and proposed terms) and a link to your SOC2/attestation. Monica/Vivek, if you can prepare the SOC2 summary and a short data flow diagram that’d be ideal.

—Daniel
Daniel Cho
Head of Procurement | ACME Commerce
